_meta.authored: AUTHORED from the engagement analysis, not captured from a client intake form. No raw intake form exists for this engagement. Form fields are reconstructed from statements in the source document; the derived competitive set and the expected conclusion are taken from it directly. The per-dimension expected levels are an ASSISTANT MAPPING of that conclusion onto the six calibrated dimensions - they are not a recorded client label. The BAND, not the dimension vector, is the bar (spec 10.6).
_meta.expected_conclusion: Reason-to-purchase not strong; position must be earned first (spec 10.1)
_meta.notes: Failing entrant, not a promising one. Launched from six former Gong Cha outlets; now three visible. The 'local + healthier' wedge is shared, copyable and contradicted by the product's own reviews. CHAGEE is the category's crown (~46 SG stores, 4.7-4.9 stars, 900-1600+ reviews per store).

form.category: Bubble tea and tea-based drinks, Singapore. Milk tea, fruit tea, pure tea, a soy-milk-tea line, and snack pairings. Drinks designed to land at HPB Nutri-Grade B or C.
form.positioning_sentence: A tea brand that belongs to Singapore - local, and healthier than the imports.
form.differentiator: We are founded by a Singaporean team and our story is local. Our drinks are formulated to be lower in sugar, landing at Nutri-Grade B or C, so a customer can drink them more often without the sugar they would get from an imported brand. We also do a soy-milk tea line that the big chains do not have.
form.undercut_on: Taste and quality. Reviews say our drinks come across as watery and syrup-based rather than fresh, that the pearls are poorly textured, and that the price is not worth it. A customer who wants an indulgence buys from CHAGEE instead.
form.your_price_point: Mid-market, comparable to other chains but below the premium tea-expert tier.
form.their_price_point: CHAGEE and the premium chains sell at a similar or higher price with far stronger product reviews.

customer_description: Singapore bubble-tea drinkers, mostly under 35, buying in malls and near campuses. The indulgence-led drinker is the majority; a smaller health-conscious segment wants lower sugar.

derived_competitive_set.derivation_method: Derived from the SG bubble-tea category: store locators, review volume and ratings, and the outlet set the brand actually trades in.

members: drinking nothing - water, kopi, or a canned drink
tier_0_default.why: Most thirst occasions are not solved by bubble tea.

tier_1_cheap_substitute.price_floor: Hawker drinks and Mixue sit far below a specialty bubble-tea cup.
tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: The cheap route solves the same thirst at a fraction of the price.

tier_2_direct_set.why: These are the chains a customer is choosing between at the same price point.

tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: CHAGEE is the reference occupant: ~46 SG stores opened within about two years, 4.7-4.9 stars with 900-1,600+ reviews per store, 200+ staff, targeting 70 stores; Nasdaq-listed (CHA) with 7,500+ stores globally. It positions as a tea expert rather than a bubble-tea brand.
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: It owns the craft-premium tier and the cultural-premium story.

members: dessert and bakery chains with a drink line
tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: A coffee or dessert purchase substitutes for the same treat occasion.

members: none - no professional specifies a bubble-tea brand
tier_5_professional_route.why: There is no intermediary in this category.

tier_6_indirect.why: A category-wide shift toward lower sugar can help or strand a brand depending on execution.

_expected.why: A failing entrant with no durable reason-to-purchase. Defensibility is the weakest dimension: the local story is shared with LiHO and KOI and is time-limited, and the healthier story is copyable. Market headroom is favourable - tea demand is real and growing - which is precisely the dimension that must not be allowed to mask the rest. Demand reach sits at 3 because the three surviving outlets are trading and therefore demonstrably reach buyers.
